{align=center} **Cell Covers (CC) **

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes. 

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows. 

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading. 

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present. 

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Newspaper article in Main News **

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!! 

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

| Revenue | 800 000 |
| --- | ---: |
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |
| of which: Inventory | 5 000 |
| Current liabilities | 15 000 |

Consider how the changes in the following **three **government legal controls could affect CC.

- Increase in the minimum wage
- More controls over what can be stated in advertisements
- No waste plastic can be sent to landfill sites

Which change is likely to have the greatest effect on profit? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
An increase in the minimum wage would likely raise CC's costs, as they currently pay their 10 skilled production workers just above the minimum wage **[Ap]**. With plans to hire two additional workers for their new personalised covers **[Ap]**, this could further increase labour costs. CC might need to raise prices or find ways to increase productivity to maintain profits **[An]**

More controls over claims made in advertising could impact CC's marketing strategy. Their current advertisement states, "Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!!"**[Ap]** If this claim is found to be misleading, CC may need to change their advertising approach, which could incur costs for market research **[An]**

The ban on sending waste plastic to landfill sites would require CC to find alternative methods of disposing of the large amount of plastic waste **[Ap]** it generates. However, recycling this waste could significantly increase their costs because it may involve investing in new equipment or outsourcing to specialist recycling companies **[An]**

The ban on sending waste plastic to landfill sites is likely to have the greatest effect on profit **[E]**. It would require a complete overhaul of CC's waste management processes, affecting both their standardised covers and new personalised range **[Ap]**. While the other changes are significant, they may be easier to adapt to through gradual wage increases or changing marketing strategies **[E]**. The waste management issue, however, affects all of CC's production process and would require immediate and costly solutions **[E]**

> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Increase in the minimum wage**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - May boost worker motivation → higher productivity and quality
>     - If CC already pays just above minimum wage → costs may remain unchanged
>     - Higher wages increase disposable income for employees → potential rise in cover sales
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Wage bill rises as 10 workers earn more → higher operating costs
>     - Competing employers may lure staff if CC holds wages flat → recruitment and training costs increase
> - **More controls over advertisement claims**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - If CC’s current adverts are truthful → no revision needed → zero extra cost
>     - Competitors must also comply → CC’s superior product claims stand out → possible sales gain
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Misleading adverts must be reworked → may become less appealing → potential drop in sales
> - **Ban on sending plastic waste to landfill**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Recycling focus can cut long-term raw-material costs → boost margin
>     - Competitors with higher disposal costs become less competitive → CC may capture market share
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Proper plastic recycling incurs higher disposal fees → increases short-term costs
>     - Training 10 workers and changing processes → upfront expense and possible production delays
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Minimum wage rise has the greatest profit impact due to significantly higher wage costs
>   - Plastic-waste controls impose moderate costs but offer long-term savings and competitive advantage
>   - Advertisement rules carry minimal cost if CC’s claims are already accurate, making this the least impactful change

{align=center} **Everyone Theatre (ET) **

Zane and Zaara are both actors. They plan to start up a theatre in a low-income area of Main City. Zane and Zaara believe that helping the community is as important as being successful entrepreneurs. 

The theatre will be a private sector business and Zane and Zaara have to decide whether to start up as an unincorporated business (partnership) or as a limited company. Zane is planning to prepare a cash-flow forecast for the first year. Zaara knows they will need to set business objectives for the theatre and also decide on a leadership style to use when managing employees. ET will have 24 part-time employees as shown in the organisational chart in Appendix 1. 

Zane and Zaara plan to put on performances in the evenings for local people and tourists. There will be 100 seats in the theatre but not all the seats will be sold if the price is too high. The Marketing Manager, Zaara, will need to decide which performances to put on, what price to charge and which refreshments to sell. Zaara will also need to decide between the two possible options for the first performance when the theatre opens. Information on the two options is shown in Appendix 2.

In the daytime the theatre building will be used by Daycare, a local social enterprise. Daycare takes care of young children up to the age of 5 so that low-income family members can go out to work. It also provides education for the children which helps their development and progress before they start school. Some of Daycare’s objectives are different to those of ET

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Proposed organisational chart for the theatre**

Note: The numbers in brackets are the number of part-time employees who work in each department

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Forecast data for the two possible options for ET’s first performance at the theatre**

| For each performance | **Option 1** | **Option 2** |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Number of actors/employees | 7 | 24 |
| Average wage cost per actor/employee | \$30 | \$10 |
| All other costs including scenery, costumes and promotion | \$1000 | \$2000 |
| Forecast revenue assuming all 100 seats are sold | \$1000 | \$2500 |

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Email from Zane to Zaara**

**To: Zaara **

**From: Zane **

**Date: 1 April 2023**

We want to support the local community and we need to make decisions about the following. 

Should we: 

- Pay fair wages even though they may be higher than those paid by competing theatres?
- Only buy costumes produced in the local community?
- Purchase all refreshments from suppliers that do not pollute the environment?

Consider the following **three **ethical issues for the theatre.

- Paying fair wages to employees
- Only buying costumes produced in the local community
- Purchasing all refreshments from suppliers that do not pollute the environment

Which ethical issue is likely to have the biggest effect on ET? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Paying fair wages to its 24 part-time employees **[Ap]** would increase ET's costs significantly. This could force ET to increase ticket prices, potentially reducing demand and revenue. However, fair wages may motivate employees to work harder, improving the quality of performances and attracting more customers **[An]**

Only buying local costumes would support the community, aligning with Zane and Zaara's goal. This could generate goodwill and attract more local customers to fill the 100 seats **[Ap]**. However, costume quality may be lower, impacting performance quality **[An]**

Purchasing eco-friendly refreshments shows environmental responsibility but may limit choices and be more expensive. This could slightly reduce refreshment sales **[Ap] **if increased costs are passed on to customers, though these are a minor part of ET's total revenue **[An]**

In conclusion, fair wages will likely have the largest financial impact on ET's costs and potential revenues **[E]**. It also most directly affects ET's 24 employees and the local community, making it the ethical issue with the biggest overall effect on the theatre's operations and success **[E]**. As ET is in a low-income area of Main City **[Ap]**, fair wages could boost the local economy and increase people's ability to afford theatre tickets **[Ap]**, further boosting ET's reputation **[E]**

> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Provides local people with higher incomes → raises living standards → expands pool of customers able to buy theatre seats → revenue up
>     - Higher wages boost staff motivation → better performance quality → stronger audience satisfaction

{align=center} **MainCity Bakery (MB)**

MainCity Bakery (MB) MB is a small bakery that produces bread. Yasin started the bakery 6 months ago with help from the government. Yasin needed a business plan to support his application for government help. An extract from the business plan Yasin produced is shown in Appendix 1. The market research was carried out by Yasin. He asked a small sample of family and friends to fill in a questionnaire. Yasin’s business plan also contained forecast data. MB’s bread is freshly-made every day in the bakery, which is located at the back of MB’s small shop. The bread is then sold the same day. Yasin has 2 employees to help him produce the bread and 1 employee to serve customers in the shop. All employees work 5 days a week and are paid the legal minimum wage. Yasin uses a democratic leadership style. Yasin needs to keep costs low to be competitive. He uses packaging that cannot be recycled. Yasin also buys the cheapest ingredients, most of which are imported. He is planning to use lean production in the bakery but he has to decide which method to use. MB’s main competitors advertise that they only use ingredients from local suppliers. Yasin is thinking of changing the suppliers he uses for ingredients and packaging. He wants MB to have a good ethical image which he could use in advertising. Yasin plans to start making cakes. He is considering two options as outlined in Appendix 2. MB’s fixed costs will increase as there will be additional expenses whichever option he chooses.

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Extract from Yasin’s business plan for MB**

| Section | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Market research | Questionnaire results are as follows:- Bread is eaten by all age groups
- Of the sample asked:
- 85% want products made using ingredients from local suppliers
- 70% want to purchase cakes as well as bread from a bakery |
| Resources | - \$10 000 to buy bakery equipment
- Rent for the bakery and shop each month
- \$3000 for start-up supplies and ingredients |

{align=center} **Appendix 2**

{align=center} **Forecast data for MB’s cake options**

|   | **Option 1 Small cupcakes** | **Option 2 Large birthday cakes** |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Monthly sales of cakes | 4000 | 100 |
| Variable cost per cake | \$0.50 | \$10 |
| Additional fixed cost per month | \$3000 | \$3000 |
| Price per cake | \$2 per cupcake | \$60 per birthday cake |
| Gross profit margin | 75% | 83.33% |
| Sales growth | Low | High |

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Packaging supplier advertisement**

{align=center} We only supply packaging made from sustainable sources. This will keep your products fresh and protect the environment. We can deliver your packaging when you need it.

Consider the following **three **ways Yasin could improve the ethical image of MB.

- Buying all ingredients from local suppliers.
- Using only environmentally friendly packaging.
- Increasing wage rates to 20% above the legal minimum wage.

Which way would be most effective? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2022-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
By switching to local suppliers, MB could compete directly with rivals on their ethical stance. It aligns with Yasin's desire to develop an ethical image **[Ap]** and, as 85% of people surveyed want products made using local ingredients **[Ap]**,  it would be very popular with customers and could significantly boost MB's image and sales. It is likely, though, to be more expensive than buying cheaper, imported ingredients **[An]**

Currently, MB uses packaging that cannot be recycled **[Ap]**, which is not sustainable. Switching to eco-friendly packaging would reduce waste and appeal to environmentally conscious customers **[An]**, and there is an available supplier of sustainable packaging **[Ap]**. However, this might increase costs and some customers may not notice the change in packaging **[An]**

Increasing wages to 20% above the legal minimum could improve employee motivation and reduce staff turnover within the bakery **[Ap]**. This could lead to better quality products, indirectly improving MB's image **[An]**. However, it would increase costs significantly and may not be as visible to customers as the other options **[An]**

Overall, the improved ethical image and ability to compete with local rivals on social responsibility could justify the higher costs of local ingredients **[E]**. Sourcing locally offers the best balance of meeting customer preferences, matching competitor strategies, and creating a visible ethical stance **[**`equation`E**]** for customers of bakery products** [Ap]**. This approach is most likely to enhance MB's reputation and attract environmentally conscious customers than the other options **[**`equation`E**]**

>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Buying all ingredients from local suppliers**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Ingredients sourced locally → no imports → lower transport pollution and carbon footprint
>     - Supports local businesses (e.g. flour mills) → strengthens community relations
>     - Cheaper and quicker deliveries → fresher ingredients and lower logistics cost
>     - Meets customer demand (85 % surveyed prefer local sourcing) → aligns with market preferences
>     - Matches competitor practices → no loss of competitive position
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Local ingredients cost more than low-cost imports → may require higher selling prices → risk of reduced demand
>     - Limited supplier range → potential constraints on product variety and recipe flexibility
> - **Using only environmentally friendly packaging**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Enhances bakery’s green image → appeals to eco-aware consumers and new market segments
>     - Future-proofs against stricter environmental regulations → reduces compliance risk
>     - Reliable sustainable packaging supplier available (Appendix 3) → ensures continuity
>     - Lowers risk of activist or pressure-group backlash → protects reputation
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Eco-friendly packaging may offer less product protection → risk of damaged goods
>     - Time spent sourcing new packaging → less focus on core baking operations
>     - Higher packaging costs (likely 10 %+ increase) → may force price hikes → some customers may resist
> - **Increasing wages to 20 % above the legal minimum**
>

>   - Sustainable packaging boosts the bakery’s green credentials and regulatory resilience yet demands careful cost management to retain price competitiveness
>   - Above-minimum wages foster staff loyalty and productivity but should be clearly communicated to amplify reputational gains without eroding margins

{align=center} **Furniture Outdoors (FO)**

FO has been a private limited company for 20 years. It is owned and run by the Chan family and is located in country Z. In country Z the secondary sector has become relatively more important as the country has developed. FO is a manufacturer of wooden furniture that is suitable for outdoor use. Its products include tables, chairs and other outdoor furniture. 

Customers order online from the FO website. The furniture is then delivered to customers in country Z using FO’s own delivery vehicles. However, FO is considering changing to selling its furniture through either wholesalers or large retailers in country Z. 

The Chan family have the business objective of contributing to sustainable development. FO only uses sustainably sourced wood when making furniture. This is from local forests in country Z and the wood is more expensive than imported alternatives. 

For many years FO shareholders have reinvested profits to provide the finance for growth. FO recently took over 2 other furniture businesses in country Z and plans further takeovers. The Chan family plan to continue to control and manage FO after this expansion. The leadership style of these two companies is very different to that of FO and their factories are located several miles away from FO in different regions of country Z. 

FO need to manage all its resources effectively. It tries to use the same components such as nails, brackets and paint for all its furniture designs. It is important to not run out of raw materials and so orders to suppliers must be carefully planned to avoid late deliveries. FO want to keep wastage of materials to a minimum. FO also need to consider how many employees are required to complete each order.

{align=center} **Appendix 1 - FO website advertisement**

**FO - the only business to go to when you need new outdoor furniture for your garden. **

FO produce a range of high quality furniture to meet all your needs for fashionable, well designed outdoor furniture. Be reassured our furniture is only made from the highest quality wood from sustainable forests. 

Our furniture is only available online so order today and have your furniture delivered in the next few weeks. Email any questions to us and we will reply quickly.

{align=center} **Appendix 2**

{align=center} **Extract of cost, selling price and sales data for one of FO’s products**

| **Fixed cost per month** | \$10 000 |
| --- | :---: |
| **Variable cost per table** | \$125 |
| **Selling price per table** | \$250 |
| **Forecasts sales for tables per month** | 100 |

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Newspaper article from the Daily News April 2021 **

{align=center} **Sustainable production needed to save the planet **

A report from the International Committee for the Planet states that manufacturers must find more sustainable ways to produce their products as global warming is becoming more of an issue. 

The report suggests three main ways manufacturers can change: 

- Only use raw materials from sources that replace what they have used. This is estimated to raise variable costs by 20%
- Only use packaging that can be recycled. Costs are estimated to increase but the selling price may not rise by more than 10%
- Only use electric vehicles to deliver products. The cost of buying electric vehicles is more than petrol or diesel vehicles. Using electric vehicles could enable variable costs to be reduced by 5%.

Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 and other information. Consider the following **three **ways FO could use to contribute to sustainable development:

- only use raw materials from sources that replace what they have used
- only use packaging that can be recycled
- only use electric vehicles to deliver products.

Which way should FO choose to maximise profit? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-june-2021-insert-paper-2-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Using raw materials from sustainable sources aligns with FO's current practice of using sustainably sourced wood from local forests  **[Ap]**. However, this would increase variable costs by 20% (\$25 per table)  **[Ap]**, potentially reducing profit unless FO raises prices or increases sales volume **[An]**

Recycled packaging could enhance FO's eco-friendly image  **[An]**. The cost increase is estimated to be less than 10% of the selling price (maximum \$25 per table)  **[Ap]**. As FO sells large furniture items, packaging costs may not significantly impact overall profitability  **[An]**

Switching to electric vehicles for deliveries would require a large initial investment but could reduce variable costs by 5% (\$6.25 per table) **[Ap]**. This aligns with FO's sustainability objective and could be a unique selling point, potentially increasing sales **[An]**

To maximise profit, FO should choose to use recycled packaging **[E]**. This option has the least impact on costs while still contributing to its sustainability objective **[Ap]**. It allows FO to market itself as environmentally responsible, potentially attracting more 'green' customers without significantly increasing expenses **[E]**. The other options, while beneficial for sustainability, would have a greater impact on costs and may require substantial changes to FO's operations or pricing strategy **[E]**

>     - Running costs fall by 5 % → saves about \$6.25 per delivery
>     - Unique selling point → differentiates FO in the market
>     - Long-term cost savings → lower total operating expense over vehicle life
>     - Meets FO’s sustainability goals → reduces air pollution
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Higher initial purchase cost → significant upfront investment
>     - Electric fleet replacement planning required → potential operational risk at lease end
> - **Conclusion **
> 
>   - Raw materials deliver the strongest reputation boost and pricing power but eliminate current profit unless price or volume rises
>   - Recyclable packaging reinforces green branding and may draw ethical customers yet adds packaging expense that could curb demand
>   - Electric vehicles underpin FO’s sustainability USP and lower running costs but demand substantial capital outlay
>   - FO should balance immediate margin impact and investment needs against long-term brand enhancement and cost savings to choose the best mix

parts.problem_md: Do you think a business being ethical will always lead to lower profits? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:

This can help offset the increased costs of using ethically-sourced materials, for example, **[An]** so overall profit margin may not change**,** and the better reputation gained could result in additional sales** [An]**

However, some firms may struggle to find ethically-sourced raw materials, especially locally** [K]**. The long delivery distances and extra transport costs **[An]** may push prices so high that demand is reduced** [An]** and profits fall

Therefore, being ethical can benefit a business, as in the long term revenue** **and profits may increase ** [E]**. However, some customers may not be prepared to pay the higher price for the ethical behaviour, particularly for everyday low-cost items **[E] **so profits are likely to fall

By responding to environmental pressures, additional revenue gained could be used to offset any extra costs, such as using sustainable raw materials** [E]**.
